data.why: The app ships sample_data/ with real melt-curve/peak TXT pairs and a built-in 'Load sample data' sidebar button that reads them directly, so no synthetic data is needed; the same files are also copied out for the browser agent to exercise manual upload if desired.

goals: Load an experiment's melt-curve TXT exports and confirm all expected wells were discovered and paired with their peak files
Inspect per-well melt curve and −dF/dT melt-peak overlays to judge amplicon specificity (single vs multiple Tm peaks)
Identify and exclude outlier technical replicates, either manually or via automatic RMSE/Tm-deviation thresholds
Compare replicate-averaged curves with ±1 SD shading to assess reproducibility across a well
Normalize and smooth curves to make Tm comparisons across wells visually consistent
Export a summary table and plots (PNG/PDF/HTML) documenting the final melt-curve analysis

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-evidenced tree of the Streamlit melt-curve viewer: phases, labels and nine sampled screens all match the app and the replay, and failures (Kaleido export, Tm never computed, exclusions cleared when the well filter changes) are reported honestly. Before filing it needs a summary-table feature, f4 split in two, clearer marking that the peak-Tm outlier method was never shown working, and a note that the README's recommended HTML version and ZIP loading are not covered.
